newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-CHRONOLOGY OF SUPER LEAGUE BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-CHRONOLOGY OF SUPER LEAGUE BATTLE.

text.p: The battle for control of rugby
league reached a turning point on Friday with a court decision
clearing the way for media magnate Rupert Murdoch's rebel Super
League to begin in Australia in 1997.
Chronology of events:
Nov 4, 1994 - Media reveals Murdoch's Super League plans.
Nov 10, 1994 - Australian Rugby League says 18 of its
existing clubs have signed loyalty agreements tying them to the
ARL for the following five years.
Feb 6, 1995 - Rival Australian media magnate Kerry Packer
attends crisis meeting of ARL clubs and declares his support.
April 19, 1995 - ARL criticises Britain's Rugby Football
League for signing deal to play with Super League, joining New
Zealand and several Pacific nations.
Sept 25, 1995 - Murdoch launches Federal Court action
challenging the validity of loyalty agreements.
Feb 23, 1996 - Federal Court finds against Super League,
Justice James Burchett ruling in favour of loyalty agreements.
Feb 28, 1996 - ARL puts back start of season by two weeks
after Burchett grants temporary injunction to stop Super League
kicking off in early March ahead of his complete set of orders.
March 11, 1996 - Burchett delivers sweeping orders against
Super League, banning it until 2000 and tying clubs and players
to the ARL for the same period.
March 19, 1996 - The 311 rebel Super League players threaten
to start their own competition after peace talks fail. Four days
later the Federal Court orders the players to abandon the plan.
May 23, 1996 - Murdoch launches appeal against the February
Federal Court ruling and subsequent orders.
Oct 4, 1996 - A three-man Federal Court appeals panel
overturns Burchett's ruling, freeing Super League to begin.
